sections.html:
Christian County is large: 724 square miles, the second-largest in Kentucky by area. Hopkinsville holds the courthouse, and Crofton, LaFayette, Oak Grove and Pembroke are the smaller cities. Central time applies, the Clarksville metro area reaches in, and Fort Campbell lies along the southern side.

Housing here leans toward rentals. The 2020 census counted 26,435 households in 29,206 housing units, with 49.9 percent owner-occupied and 50.1 percent renter-occupied. Vacancy stood at 9.5 percent, and about 71 percent of people lived in places the census calls urban. Many sellers are therefore landlords, and military moves tied to Fort Campbell can leave little time between an order and a closing.

sections.h2: Who to call for each tax or records task
sections.html:
The county clerk at 511 South Main Street in Hopkinsville handles most seller paperwork, with weekday hours from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm. Its phone menu routes the usual requests.

Christian County Clerk phone routing for sellers
What you needNumberNotes
Main clerk line(270) 887-4105Menu extension 3 covers copies of a deed or a plat
Legal records division(270) 887-4109Deeds, mortgages, tax liens and releases filed since 1797
Delinquent tax sale questions(270) 887-4109Same line as the tax sale registration notice
Probate and court records(270) 889-6539Justice Center, not the clerk

For what the house is worth, phone the Christian County PVA. For the current bill, the sheriff's tax office is the place. A missing number? The clerk's main line can redirect you. The legal records division keeps deeds back to 1797, which helps when a chain of title crosses several generations of owners.

Renting the unit out doesn't shift the tax to your tenant. The assessment date makes it your personal debt, and any year left unpaid travels with the parcel into a sale. Landlords gain the most from early payment, since 2 percent off on several rentals adds up. If a servicer or property manager pays your bill, confirm each year that the payment actually went through.

Fort Campbell families are zoned to the federal DoDEA schools, while Christian County Public Schools serve most other households. Buyers ask about schools early, so know which system your address falls in.

Dates come from KRS 134.015. Pay in full by November 1 and you get 2 percent off. Pay by year end and you owe the printed figure. January costs 5 percent more, and anything after that costs 10 percent more. Once the bill moves to the clerk, the sheriff's fees and a clerk commission are added, and the state's sample shows the total growing by about a quarter.

If your house lies inside Hopkinsville, Oak Grove or another city, ask that city whether it bills its own tax and on what dates.

Your first step is a conference with the Christian County PVA, held while the roll is open for public review. Expect the PVA to walk you through how the value was set. Phone conferences are available on request.

No deal? File a written appeal with the county clerk by the workday following the end of the review. The local board sits roughly a month on and looks at comparable sales, contracts, insurance policies and, for rentals, income and expense statements. A paid representative has to be an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, broker, appraiser or your own employee, with written authority from you.

  • The board can raise a value as well as lower it, so bring evidence for your number.
  • The state's tax appeals board hears later appeals, but only from owners who first used the county board.
  • Payment on the value you claim stays due while the appeal runs.

Expect a single sale each summer, run by the clerk. The county website lists the date and a registration cutoff a few weeks before. The legal records division at (270) 887-4109 can give you this year's schedule.

State rules frame the timing. Bills move to the clerk on April 15 and the sale must come 90 to 135 days later. The county attorney sends notices in between, and the clerk advertises the list no fewer than 30 days before the sale. A buyer who wants more than three bills in the county, or more than five statewide, must register with the Department of Revenue 60 days before the sale.

Once a bill is a certificate of delinquency, a lien sits on the parcel and interest of 1 percent a month plus clerk and attorney fees accrue. Pay before the sale and the matter is closed. Pay after it and you're dealing with whoever bought the lien.

If you're 65 or older, or totally disabled, and the house is your residence, you can claim it. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and it comes off the assessed value ahead of the tax calculation. Apply at the Christian County PVA with proof of age or disability. Disability claims renew each year, except for owners with a service-connected disability and owners with permanent findings from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Thinking of renting the house out or moving? Ask the PVA what that does to the exemption first.

sections.h2: Selling a Christian County house that owes tax
sections.html:
Pull payoff figures before you set a price. The sheriff's tax office can state a current balance, and the clerk can say whether an earlier year was filed as a delinquency. The title company subtracts both at closing and records the release.

Penalties land on fixed dates whether or not you're mid-move. A purchaser willing to take the house without repairs can close on your date and clear the tax from your proceeds, which beats catching up in cash while you pack. Before agreeing to a price, ask any buyer to show how the tax payoff and lien release will appear on the closing statement.

If a tenant is living in the house, tell the buyer and the closing agent early. Rent, deposits and the lease terms all need to be handled in the contract, and the tax split should follow the deed date.

Sellers relocating on military orders sometimes need to close by a set date. Tell the closing agent that date at the start so the payoff letters, lien release and recording are lined up in time. Ask the sheriff and the clerk how long each will take to produce a written balance, because the clerk's legal records division also handles deed copies and releases and can get busy.

faqs.q: What is the county clerk's address in Christian County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The clerk is at 511 South Main Street, Hopkinsville, KY 42240, phone (270) 887-4105, on weekdays between 8:00 am and 4:00 pm. The legal records division is at (270) 887-4109.

faqs.q: When is the Christian County delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: Once a year in summer. The county website posts the date and a registration deadline ahead of time, so call (270) 887-4109 for the current schedule.

faqs.q: What happens to a Christian County tax bill after April 15?
faqs.a: The bill moves from the sheriff to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien attaches to the parcel. Interest of 1 percent a month and clerk and attorney fees are then added.

faqs.q: Do I still owe tax if a renter lives in my Christian County house?
faqs.a: Yes. Property tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, no matter who occupies the house.

faqs.q: Can a Christian County owner past 65 reduce the tax?
faqs.a: Yes, through the homestead exemption, which is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the Christian County PVA and show proof of age.
